data.title: Favicon
data.tagline: A small icon browsers use to identify a website
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish a Favicon from a header Logo and a UI action icon, then verify the Favicon in browser surfaces.
data.description: After a site opens, the browser can show it in tabs, bookmarks, and history so people can recognize the site among many pages. A working header Logo does not prove that the browser received a Favicon; inspect the actual browser surfaces.

learning.assumes: You have seen a small site icon in a browser tab, bookmark, or history list.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish a Favicon from a header Logo and a UI action icon, then verify the Favicon in browser surfaces.

distinctions.label: Logo
distinctions.explanation: Favicon appears in browser tabs, bookmarks, and history; a Logo usually appears in page content to identify a brand.

distinctions.label: UI icon
distinctions.explanation: Favicon identifies the site; an Icon communicates a function, object, or status inside the page.

explanation.title: It identifies a site in the browser
explanation.text: Tabs, bookmarks, and history can show the same Favicon so people can recognize a website quickly. It does not explain an action inside the page.

explanation.title: Verify the real browser result
explanation.text: After publishing, confirm that the linked asset is reachable and inspect it in tabs, bookmarks, and history; an old cache may keep the previous asset visible for a while.

data.boundary: Favicon is used in browser surfaces; a Logo is a brand mark in page content; an Icon communicates a search, close, or other function. They may share a visual source, but changing one does not automatically change the others.

lessonPractice.title: After the header Logo changes, the browser tab still shows the old icon. What should you check first?

options.label: Check the Favicon asset and rel=icon configuration, then account for possible caching
options.feedback: Correct. The header Logo and browser Favicon are separate paths, so inspect the asset, relation, and browser cache.

options.label: Keep adjusting the Header Logo until the tab changes by itself
options.feedback: The Header owns the brand entry in the page; it does not automatically replace the browser tab icon.

options.label: Replace a toolbar action icon with the new brand shape
options.feedback: A UI action icon communicates an operation and is separate from the Favicon that identifies the site in the browser.

data.agentPrompt: Replace the site's Favicon while leaving the header Logo and toolbar action icons unchanged. Check the asset referenced by rel=icon, then verify the browser tab, bookmark, and history after deployment. If the old icon remains, report the caching evidence and the next verification step.
